value.body: An aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) keeps aircraft safe to fly by inspecting, servicing and repairing them and, once licensed, certifying that work. Employers include airlines, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) firms, helicopter and charter operators, and flying schools. Work happens in hangars and on the ramp, often in shifts.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: DGCA-approved AME course, or an engineering degree plus experience

items.label: Licence
items.note: Categories such as B1 (mechanical) and B2 (avionics); needs DGCA module exams and logged practical experience

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Two routes exist: a DGCA-approved AME training programme, or an engineering degree (aerospace, mechanical or electronics) followed by DGCA module exams and supervised work experience. B.Tech graduates often join airlines or MROs as trainee or technical engineers and build experience toward a licence.

value.title: At a glance
items: A B.Tech alone does not let you certify aircraft — the DGCA licence does.
Shift and night work is common.
Next roles: licensed engineer, shift supervisor, quality or planning roles in an MRO.
